deities: Sri Bhimeswara Swamy (Shiva - ~9-ft crystal-textured lingam in a two-storeyed sanctum)
Sri Manikyamba Devi (Shakti; Ashtadasha Shakti Peetha)
Sub-shrines: Ganapati (Dundi/Thandava), Subrahmanya, Nandi, Navagrahas, Dakshinamurthy, Surya-Chandra, Lakshmi Narayana (kshetrapalaka), Sapta Matrikas, Kala Bhairava, Annapurna, Kanaka Durga

history.period: 9th-10th century CE (inscriptions; reign of Eastern Chalukya king Bhima, c. 892-902)
history.summary: One of the five Pancharama Kshetras of Shiva and the 12th of the Ashtadasha (18) Shakti Peethas, where Sati's left cheek is said to have fallen. Tradition says the lingam was installed by Surya (the Sun god) and worshipped by the Saptarishis; it is believed to have formed from a fragment of the Shiva-lingam broken in the Tarakasura battle (Pancharama legend). The site is also associated with Daksha's yajna. Inscriptions reveal construction by Eastern Chalukya king Bhima between the 9th and 10th centuries CE; the big mandapam was later built by Ganga Mahadevi (Eastern Ganga period) and the architecture blends Chalukyan and Chola styles. Maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India as a Monument of National Importance. The Sapta Godavari pushkarini (tank) lies in front. NOTE: sources give the lingam height variously as 9 ft, 10 ft and 14 ft - verify.

name: Sri Bhimeswara Swamy Temple
town_description: Draksharamam (also Daksharamam) is an ancient temple town in Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district, about 28 km from Kakinada, 60 km from Rajahmundry and 6 km from Ramachandrapuram on the Rajahmundry-Yanam route. Known as Dakshina Kashi, it is a twin Shaiva-Shakti centre (Pancharama + Shakti Peetha) that draws pilgrims year-round, especially on Shivaratri.

travel.airport: Rajahmundry Airport (~55-60 km) is the nearest; Visakhapatnam is farther (verify distances).
travel.railway: Nearest major railway station Rajahmundry (RJY, ~60 km, verify); Ramachandrapuram (~6 km) is the nearest town.
travel.road: On the Rajahmundry-Yanam road; motorable roads to the temple; Sapta Godavari tank in front of the complex.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maha Shivaratri (Feb/Mar) and Navaratri draw the largest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-12:00 noon and 3:00-8:00 PM; on Masa Shivaratri and Maha Shivaratri open throughout 6:00 AM-8:00 PM (per templeconnect - verify).
